column1: # Expected keyword content per term, per ANNO-1b. Ground truth, not generated output.
# One row per expectation: termKey <TAB> kind <TAB> text, where kind is
#   NAME        a published name of the term
#   DEFINITION  a published definition of the term
#   UNRESOLVED  the captured response is not a term (the provider answered 404); no names exist.
# Every value is transcribed from the published fields of the captured responses under
# annotation/providers/. The rows were first transcribed on 2026-11-13 from the provider's v1
# the v2 bodies that replaced it carry the same content as flat, IRI-keyed fields (`label`,
# `IAO_0000115`), and the rows were re-checked against those on 2026-11-16. No v1 capture survives,
# so the v1 field names above are history, not a fixture.
# Since ANNO-1g the three `go:` rows are transcribed from the QuickGO captures
# is what the term chain wires for the GO prefix; the OLS4 go captures are no longer read here.
# Values are de-duplicated case-insensitively, first spelling kept, because that is
# the rule the keyword text itself follows.
# Regenerate only from a fresh capture, by hand: a changed expectation is a decision, not a diff.

Note that, in addition to forming the root of the biological process ontology, this term is recommended for the annotation of gene products whose biological process is unknown. When this term is used for annotation, it indicates that no information was available about the biological process of the gene product annotated as of the date the annotation was made; the evidence code 'no data' (ND), is used to indicate this.

A biological process is the execution of a genetically-encoded biological module or program. It consists of all the steps required to achieve the specific biological objective of the module. A biological process is accomplished by a particular set of molecular functions carried out by specific gene products (or macromolecular complexes), often in a highly regulated manner and in a particular temporal sequence.
